old_page_facts.fact: Failure 5: errors compound through joins; 10x at the bottom of three joins is 1000x at the top; fundamental weakness
old_page_facts.source: Leis et al., PVLDB 9(3) 2015: misestimates by a factor of 1000 or more routine; underestimation tendency

old_page_facts.fact: Failure 6: cost constants not matching hardware; random_page_cost 4 wrong on NVMe, 1.1 common setting
old_page_facts.correction: Default is 4.0, but current docs give no SSD value and justify 4 by caching; 1.1 is practice, not a documented standard; change only with measurements

old_page_facts.fact: How to work: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), compare estimated vs actual rows at every node; lowest divergence is the problem; buffers show cache vs disk
old_page_facts.note: Added: multiply by loops; PG18 enables BUFFERS by default; timing overhead measured (67%)

old_page_facts.fact: Most failures are estimation not costing, which is why learned planners are plausible
old_page_facts.where: Reading s12; s2 'What the cost model does not know' (Leis: cost model matters much less)

old_page_facts.fact: Learned planner: 4B distillation writing Postgres plans, 1.81x geomean, 44.7% latency reduction on JOB, zero regressions when best of three, September 2026
old_page_facts.correction: rohanbansal.com/qorl (2026-09-16): model's own choice 1.40x with 7 regressions over 339 runs; best within a run 1.44x, 1 regression; best measured across three runs (up to 15 executed candidates) 1.81x, 44.7%, 0 regressions; hints via pg_hint_plan; trained on 13,646 CEB queries; untrained produced no plan for 99 of 113; $1,200 ($800 GPU, $400 API); JOB used as validation during development

old_page_facts.fact: Economics: generating and measuring candidates costs more than planning; pays only for repeated analytic queries, not transactional traffic
Best resource: Use The Index, Luke (composite ordering, sargability, covering indexes, reading EXPLAIN)
Habit: multiply number of operations by the cost of one and compare with measured latency
